title: Tooth Types and FDI Numbering
subtitle: The system for permanent and primary teeth

slides.title: Number of Teeth
bullets: Permanent teeth: 32 in a complete dentition (including wisdom teeth)
As a child grows, the primary teeth are replaced by permanent teeth

slides.title: The FDI System
bullets: Each tooth is designated by a two-digit number
First digit — the quadrant (one quarter of the dentition)
Second digit — the tooth’s position, counted from the midline
Quadrants 1–4 for permanent teeth, 5–8 for primary teeth

slides.title: Example: The Molar
bullets: Molars are located in the posterior part of the dental arch
They have a large chewing surface
The number of roots varies by tooth and jaw
slides.caption: Chewing surface of a molar

slides.title: Key Points
bullets: The first digit indicates the quadrant

quiz.q: How many permanent teeth are there (including wisdom teeth)?
quiz.explanation: A complete permanent dentition has 32 teeth.

quiz.q: How many primary teeth are there?
What does the first digit of an FDI number indicate?
quiz.explanation: The first digit indicates the quadrant, one quarter of the dentition.
Molars have a large chewing surface and grind food.

quiz.q: Which digits designate the quadrants for permanent teeth?
quiz.explanation: 1–4 for permanent teeth, 5–8 for primary teeth.
